items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Jim Europe, who was the leader of the 365th Engineers band during the first World War, was recognised as being the first Negros to play jazz in Europe in 1917.

ctx.x: in B Flat. He showed me the way it was done but a musician must be trained to that type of situation and I was very slow at transposing. So Cosy who could copy things from records and write them, wrote my parts in the keys they were supposed to be in and I had no troubles after that.

Cricket had always been a first chair man and had come to Europe with Sam Wooding's orchestra in the early 1920's. Sam Wooding was the first Negro leader to bring a Negro jazz orchestra to Europe although Jim Europe, who was the leader of the 365th Engineers band during the first World War, was recognised as being the first Negros to play jazz in Europe in 1917. Jim Europe played marches, but in a ragtime way, as they were played by the marching bands in New Orleans when they were returning from the funeral of…

But Sam Wooding had an orchestra that played dance music and was composed of 12 or 14 musicians where the parade band of Jim Europe had 30 or more musicians as the usual type of parade bands. So it was thusly, Sam Wooding was recognised as being the first Negro jazz orchestra to invade the European continent. Cricket and Rudy Jackson had played in Wooding's orchestra and they were both fine musicians. I played second parts in the brass section and taking the jazz solos.
